name: Antique White
lede: Antique White is a pale, warm, yellowish white, now best known as one of the named colors of the web.

sections.title: The name
sections.body:
Paterson defines Antique White as a yellowish white adopted as a color name by web page creators [1]. It comes from the X11 and CSS color list, where it sits among the whites [1][3]. The word *antique* in color names, Paterson adds, describes things that look very old, as in antique ivory, the yellowish white of old ivory [2].

The library records Maerz and Paul using the name by 1915, on plate 11 B 3 of their 1930 dictionary, and lists it in ISCC-NBS block 73 [3]. So the name predates the web by decades; the web only made it famous [1][3].

sections.title: Neighbors
sections.body: The nearest named color in the library is [[ecru]], at a CIEDE2000 distance of 2.7, and [[antique-white]] is a near duplicate at 2.0 [3]. It is warmer than plain [[white]] and lighter than [[beige]] [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of 23,781 paintings, the color appears in 2.31% of them, as photographed [4]. It is more common than 79% of the named colors and peaks in the 1200s, where it appears in 4.2% of the paintings we hold from that century, though that century is thinly covered [4]. John Singer Sargent is its most devoted painter here, with 17 of 287 works [4]. Because these are photographs of aged, varnished canvases, a match shows a look-alike hue, not proof of a pigment [4].
